title: Move review history out of code comments; keep only current behavior and rationale
context: Comments and test names had accumulated review-round narration ("found on third review pass", etc.), creating a embedded changelog that duplicated information already in git history and Hunch decision records, making comments harder to read and prone to staleness.
decision: Strip all review-round framing from comments and test names. Comments now state only current behavior and non-obvious WHY; review history lives exclusively in commit logs and Hunch captures.
consequences: Comments become shorter and more readable
Single source of truth per information type: git/Hunch for history, code for current behavior
Reduced risk of stale cross-references surviving refactors
Easier to update rationale when behavior changes (no "but we found this on pass N" to reconcile)
alternatives_rejected: Keep review narration inline (accumulates clutter, rots as codebase evolves)
Strip comments entirely and rely only on Hunch/git (loses immediate context at edit time for non-Hunch readers)

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Keep review narration inline (accumulates clutter, rots as codebase evolves)
Strip comments entirely and rely only on Hunch/git (loses immediate context at edit time for non-Hunch readers)
